tldr: Language models can be taught to search by training on serialized search trajectories called Stream of Search (SoS), which outperforms training on optimal paths alone and enables self-improvement through policy refinement methods.
contributions: Proposing Stream of Search (SoS) as a unified language for search representing exploration, backtracking, and pruning as a flattened string
Demonstrating SoS pretraining increases search accuracy by 25% over models trained only on optimal search trajectories
Showing finetuned SoS models solve 36% of previously unsolved problems, including those unsolvable by heuristic solvers
Demonstrating language models can self-improve to flexibly use different search strategies and potentially discover new ones
methods: The authors represent search as a serialized string (Stream of Search) using explicit primitives: current state, goal state, state queue, state expansion, exploration choice, pruning, backtracking, goal check, and heuristic. They instantiate this in the Countdown game (combining 4 input numbers with arithmetic to reach a target 10-100). A GPT-Neo transformer (250M parameters, 4096 token context) is pretrained from scratch on 500,000 search trajectories generated by 12 symbolic search strategies (BFS/DFS variants with sum and multiply heuristics). The model is then finetuned using two methods: Advantage-Induced Policy Alignment (APA) with a value network and reward based on correctness and trajectory length, and Self-Taught Reasoner (STaR) expert iteration generating 100,000 correct trajectories per round.
results: The SoS model achieves 51.27% accuracy on held-out inputs versus 25.73% for the Optimal Path (OP) model. The SoS model has low error rates: 0.8% state exploration errors and ~2 arithmetic errors per trajectory. After STaR finetuning (3 iterations), the model solves an additional 5% of held-out problems beyond the base SoS model. After APA finetuning (~4000 steps with 3 reference policy resets), accuracy improves by ~6% over base SoS. The finetuned models solve 36% of previously unsolved problems from the training set, including problems that no heuristic solver can solve. The SoS model shows moderate alignment with individual symbolic strategies (highest: DFS with sum heuristic at 0.57; lowest: BFS with sum, breadth=5 at 0.27), indicating it does not predominantly adopt any single training strategy.
limitations: Only about 57% of the 500,000 generated search trajectories lead to a solution, meaning the majority of training data contains unsuccessful search attempts
The model makes approximately 2 arithmetic errors per trajectory on average, indicating imperfect internal simulation of operations
Search trajectories for games with 5 input numbers can reach 60,000 tokens, exceeding the standard context window used (4096 tokens)
The SoS model achieves slightly lower accuracy than the average of symbolic search methods used to generate training data, though it solves a harder problem by simulating transitions internally
The approach was demonstrated on a single domain (Countdown), limiting generalizability claims
